cases.reason: A signed public kind-1 post traversed five actual Geode relays through the PWA bridge. Buyer B saw the author, and the contact action selected that author in private-message navigation while the post remained public; an empty-feed state was also checked.

The browser published, discovered, and edited one satoshi, one piconero, and one raw through an actual five-relay Geode bridge. Exact atomic strings, event authorship, stable d tags, signatures, and rendered prices survived each round-trip; currency maxima and overflow were checked.

Seller withdrawal hid the offer even after the older signed event was replayed to R5. Geode rejected reinsertion under its deletion tombstone. Another author could not remove an offer; the client reducer ignored an older deletion timestamp without sending that fixture to the relay.

Expired and future-timestamp, unknown-currency, malformed, and ambiguous-address listings were filtered. The browser blocked excess precision, overflow, and unsupported-currency submissions; unsafe image URLs were not linked or fetched, and injected markup remained literal text.

Contact from the marketplace opened the correct seller conversation target without changing the displayed offer, publishing any payment/checkout/private-message event, or exposing a checkout control. The UI identifies NIP-15 as draft and states that payments/custody are not handled.

Published 20 synthetic offers per currency, edited 10, withdrew 10 and expired 10 per currency. Each of five local Geode relays served the same current replaceable heads, all 30 signed withdrawal tombstones, and identical active state before and after the logical expiry boundary. Superseded/deleted payloads were not incorrectly required to remain queryable. Bridge coverage passed earlier; this larger fixed-count batch bypassed its explicit forwarding quota.

Completed 50 PWA Hangout journeys against signed authors. Duplicate copies from five relays rendered once; the buyer changed from R5 to R4, direct-contact navigation selected the post author without sending a message, and malformed local fixtures failed closed. English and pt-BR each covered 25 journeys.

Completed 50 real PWA marketplace journeys (25 English, 25 Brazilian Portuguese) across BTC/XMR/XNO. Each published the versioned offer, browsed it from the other identity, checked public/private and no-paid labeling, opened the seller conversation, and withdrew the offer with a signed NIP-09 request.
